about.title: About Pregnancy Calculator
about.description: The Pregnancy Calculator estimates your due date, current pregnancy week, and important milestones based on your last menstrual period or conception date. Accurate pregnancy dating is essential for proper prenatal care and monitoring. Understanding pregnancy timeline helps track fetal development, schedule important appointments, and prepare for each trimester. The calculator provides comprehensive pregnancy information and milestone tracking for expectant mothers.

howTo.title: How to Use the Pregnancy Calculator

steps.title: Enter Last Menstrual Period
steps.description: Input the first day of your last menstrual period (LMP) for accurate due date calculation.

steps.title: Or Input Conception Date
steps.description: Alternatively, enter your estimated conception date if you know when conception occurred.

steps.title: View Due Date
steps.description: See your estimated due date calculated based on the standard 280-day pregnancy duration.

steps.title: Check Current Week
steps.description: View your current pregnancy week and trimester with detailed progression information.

steps.title: Track Milestones
steps.description: Monitor important pregnancy milestones and fetal development stages throughout your pregnancy.

steps.title: Plan Appointments
steps.description: Use the timeline to schedule prenatal appointments and important medical checkups.

faq.q: How accurate is the due date calculation?
faq.a: Due dates are estimates with a 2-week window of accuracy. Only about 5% of babies are born on their exact due date, with most births occurring within 2 weeks before or after the estimated date. Ultrasound dating in early pregnancy can provide more precise estimates.

faq.q: What's the difference between gestational age and fetal age?
faq.a: Gestational age is calculated from the last menstrual period and is about 2 weeks longer than fetal age. Fetal age is calculated from conception. Medical professionals typically use gestational age for pregnancy dating and milestone tracking.

faq.q: When do the trimesters begin and end?
faq.a: First trimester: weeks 1-12 (organ formation), Second trimester: weeks 13-27 (rapid growth), Third trimester: weeks 28-40 (final development and preparation for birth). Each trimester has distinct developmental milestones and medical considerations.

faq.q: Should I rely solely on this calculator for pregnancy planning?
faq.a: This calculator provides helpful estimates, but always consult healthcare providers for accurate dating and personalized care. Factors like irregular cycles, medical conditions, or conception timing can affect accuracy, requiring professional medical assessment.
